panels.title: SparkApplications currently running
panels.description: Count of SparkApplication CRs the spark-operator controller currently reports as running (spark_application_running_count) - controller-level state, independent of any single job's driver/executor pods.

panels.title: Successful completions (total)
panels.description: Cumulative count of SparkApplications the spark-operator controller has ever marked COMPLETED - a running total since the operator started, not a 24h window.

panels.title: Failed completions (total)
panels.description: Cumulative count of SparkApplications the spark-operator controller has ever marked FAILED - a running total since the operator started, not a 24h window.

panels.title: Success / failure rate (spark-operator controller)
panels.description: Rate of new completions/failures per 10-minute window, derived from the controller's cumulative counters via increase() - turns the running totals above into an actual trend.

panels.title: Success execution time (avg, seconds)
panels.description: Average execution time of successfully-completed SparkApplications, from the controller's own duration histogram - controller-reported, not scraped from individual job pods.

panels.title: Executor memory used / active tasks (live jobs)
panels.description: Only populated while a SparkApplication's driver/executor pods are actually running - scraped directly from Spark's PrometheusServlet on the driver/executor pods, so data disappears once a job completes and its pods are cleaned up.

panels.title: Task completion (live jobs)
panels.description: Completed vs failed Spark tasks from the driver/executor pods' own PrometheusServlet - only populated while a job's pods are actually running, same caveat as the Executor memory panel above.

panels.title: Driver/executor logs (ERROR/WARN)
panels.description: Log message text (extracted from fluentbit's JSON envelope, not the raw JSON line) containing 'error' or 'warn', from pods named *-driver or *-exec-* in the default namespace - Spark Operator's own driver/executor pod naming convention, since these pods carry no queryable Loki label identifying them as Spark.
